irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A WireDefinition (unlike WireRule) has no `dependsOn` field to formally record a cross-unit dependency (e.g. SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH / LIMITED_BY against an exact external section reference) when a defined TERM's own formula - not a rule's capacity - incorporates another section's usage-dependent headroom.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: UNSUPPORTED and DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE can flag the gap and name the referenced term, but neither preserves a structured, queryable pointer to the exact external section reference (e.g. 'Section 6.01(b)(12)(b)') the way dependsOn does for WireRule; the citation is only recoverable from a free-text sourceEvidence string on the UNSUPPORTED node.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: Add an optional `dependsOn` array (same shape as WireRule's) to WireDefinition so definitional formula components can carry the same structured SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH/LIMITED_BY/REQUIRES cross-references that rules can.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A WireDefinition (unlike WireRule) has no `dependsOn` field to formally record a cross-unit dependency (e.g. SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH / LIMITED_BY against an exact external section reference) when a defined TERM's own formula - not a rule's capacity - incorporates another section's usage-dependent headroom.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: UNSUPPORTED and DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE can flag the gap and name the referenced term, but neither preserves a structured, queryable pointer to the exact external section reference (e.g. 'Section 6.01(b)(12)(b)') the way dependsOn does for WireRule; the citation is only recoverable from a free-text sourceEvidence string on the UNSUPPORTED node.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: Add an optional `dependsOn` array (same shape as WireRule's) to WireDefinition so definitional formula components can carry the same structured SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH/LIMITED_BY/REQUIRES cross-references that rules can.

overallNotes: This submission covers §1.01 defined terms from 'Excluded Swap Obligation' through 'Fixed Incremental Amount' (22 distinct terms) - every term in the supplied text was extracted as its own WireDefinition; none were silently dropped.

No WireRule/WireSharedCapacity outputs were produced: this source region is a definitions article, not an operative permission/prohibition/ratio-test section, so there is no independently operative covenant rule to compile here (the definitions themselves feed rules located elsewhere, e.g. Section 6.01).

'Existing Liens' (d5): the cross-reference to Section 9.02(b) was actively resolved via getReferencedProvision, but the returned text is an Amendments/waiver-consent provision, not a Liens definition - flagged MISSING_CONTEXT as a likely mismatched/renumbered cross-reference rather than guessed.

'Expected Run Rate Benefit' (d6): actively attempted via getDefinition (both for the term itself and for 'Consolidated EBITDA'); the term is embedded deep within the very long 'Consolidated EBITDA' definition, which remains truncated at the available context/tool budget - flagged MISSING_CONTEXT rather than guessed.

'Fixed Incremental Amount' (d22): the two additive components 'unused amounts under Section 6.01(b)(12)(b)' and the full clause (e) deduction (referencing the undefined term 'Incremental Facilities' and an ambiguous 'Section 6.01(b)(1)(Z)' cross-reference already flagged as unresolvable in the provided cross-reference table) are represented as UNSUPPORTED nodes nested inside an otherwise-complete SUM/SUBTRACT tree - the computable base component ($720.0mm / 100% Consolidated EBITDA greater-of test) is preserved intact per the PARTIAL-over-discard principle.

Several terms (FCPA, FILO Tranche, Fixed Amounts, First Commitment Application Period, Existing Liens, Expected Run Rate Benefit) are pure cross-reference pointers; where the pointer resolved to usable text it is marked COMPLETE, where it did not (Existing Liens, Expected Run Rate Benefit) it is marked MISSING_CONTEXT after an actual retrieval attempt.
